title: Finite separable scheme models
statement: Let k be a field, ks a separable closure of k, and Js a finitely presented quasi-separated ks-scheme. There is a finite separable intermediate field K and a finitely presented quasi-separated K-scheme JK with a cartesian map Js to JK.

proof.text:
Every finitely presented scheme over a separable closure has a finitely presented model
 over a finite separable intermediate field. Write the separable closure as the filtered
 colimit of finitely generated subalgebras; these are fields because the extension is
 algebraic, finite because they are finitely generated, and separable because they lie in a
 separable extension. Apply finite-presentation descent to the spectra of that system.

Source: Stacks Project, Tag 01ZM (1).

lean.statement: theorem exists_finiteSeparable_schemeModel {k ks : Type u} [Field k] [Field ks] [Algebra k ks] [IsSepClosure k ks] (Js : Over (Spec (.of ks))) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation Js.hom] [QuasiCompact Js.hom] [QuasiSeparated Js.hom] : ∃ K : IntermediateField k ks, FiniteDimensional k K ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable k K ∧ ∃ (JK : Over (Spec (.of K))) (q : Js.left ⟶ JK.left), IsPullback q Js.hom JK.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K ks))) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation JK.hom ∧ QuasiCompact JK.hom ∧ QuasiSeparated JK.hom
